name: Shiloh
title: The Messianic Prince of Peace
lifespan: Prophetic designation, not a historical person with a known lifespan
summary: Shiloh is a mysterious concept found in Jacob's blessing of Judah in Genesis 49:10. The name is traditionally interpreted as a messianic title meaning 'the one to whom it belongs' or 'the bringer of peace'. Both Jewish and Christian traditions have viewed this as a prophecy about the coming Messiah, and Christians have identified Shiloh with Jesus Christ.

keyEvents.title: Jacob's Prophecy About Shiloh
keyEvents.description: On his deathbed, the patriarch Jacob prophesied that the scepter would not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples.

keyEvents.title: The Blessing of the Tribe of Judah
keyEvents.description: The prophecy about Shiloh is part of the greater blessing over Judah, where Jacob predicts that Judah will be praised by his brothers and that his father's sons will bow down before him.

keyEvents.title: David's Kingdom as Fulfillment
keyEvents.description: King David from the tribe of Judah was seen as a partial fulfillment of the Shiloh prophecy, since the kingdom was established in the tribe of Judah through an eternal covenant.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy About the Prince of Peace
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah expanded on the messianic expectation linked to Shiloh by prophesying about a child who would be called Prince of Peace, and whose rule and peace would never end on David's throne.

keyEvents.title: Jesus as Shiloh in Christian interpretation
keyEvents.description: In the New Testament, Jesus from the tribe of Judah is presented as the fulfillment of the Shiloh prophecy. He is referred to as the Lion of the tribe of Judah and the one who has received all power and authority.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel's confirmation of the Shiloh prophecy
keyEvents.description: The prophet Ezekiel seems to refer to the Shiloh prophecy when he says that the crown will be removed until he comes who has the right to it, and God will give it to him.
